excerpt: Spring drought constrained 2019 production prospects
statement: The GIEWS brief of 21 May 2019 reports that spring drought constrained Morocco's 2019 production prospects.
scope: Morocco (the brief's country); 2019 production prospects; brief of 21 May 2019
attribution: © FAO 2019 GIEWS Country Brief Morocco, reference date 21-May-2019

excerpt: To protect the livestock farmers affected by the drought, the Government announced a "Safeguard of Livestock Programme” which includes the distribution of 250 000 tonnes of subsidized barley feed.
statement: The GIEWS brief of 29 April 2020 reports that the government announced a programme for drought-affected livestock farmers that includes distributing 250 000 tonnes of subsidized barley feed.
scope: Morocco (the brief's country), drought-affected livestock farmers; brief of 29 April 2020
attribution: © FAO 2020 GIEWS Country Brief Morocco, reference date 29-April-2020

excerpt: Farmers in the most drought-affected areas decided to let their livestock graze the fields instead of harvesting.
statement: The GIEWS brief of 15 October 2020 reports that in the most drought-affected areas, farmers let their livestock graze the fields instead of harvesting.
scope: The most drought-affected areas of Morocco; 2020 season; brief of 15 October 2020
attribution: © FAO 2020 GIEWS Country Brief Morocco, reference date 15-October-2020

excerpt: Above-average cereal crop harvested in 2021
statement: The GIEWS brief of 2 August 2021 reports an above-average cereal crop harvested in Morocco in 2021.
scope: Morocco (the brief's country); the 2021 harvest; brief of 2 August 2021
attribution: © FAO 2021 GIEWS Country Brief Morocco, reference date 02-August-2021

excerpt: cumulative rainfall amounts between November 2021 and February 2022 were about half the average, causing widespread drought conditions across the country
statement: The GIEWS brief of 21 July 2022 reports that cumulative rainfall from November 2021 to February 2022 was about half the average, causing widespread drought conditions across Morocco.
scope: Morocco ('the country'); November 2021 to February 2022
attribution: © FAO 2022 GIEWS Country Brief Morocco, reference date 21-July-2022

excerpt: Abundant rainfall amounts in March and April, up to 40 percent above the average in some areas, were too late to instigate a recovery in vegetation conditions as the cereal crops had already reached the grain filling stage.
statement: The GIEWS brief of 21 July 2022 reports that March and April rainfall, up to 40 percent above average in some areas, came too late for vegetation conditions to recover because the cereal crops had already reached grain filling.
scope: Some areas of Morocco; March and April (2022, per the brief of 21 July 2022)
attribution: © FAO 2022 GIEWS Country Brief Morocco, reference date 21-July-2022

excerpt: the government announced an emergency distribution of 700 000 tonnes of subsidized barley in the regions most affected by the drought
statement: The GIEWS brief of 21 July 2022 reports that the government announced an emergency distribution of 700 000 tonnes of subsidized barley in the regions most affected by the drought.
scope: The regions of Morocco most affected by the drought; brief of 21 July 2022
attribution: © FAO 2022 GIEWS Country Brief Morocco, reference date 21-July-2022

excerpt: Barley output in 2023 is estimated at 1.35 million tonnes, 20 percent above the five-year average and almost twice the 2022 harvest.
statement: The GIEWS brief of 26 July 2023 estimates 2023 barley output at 1.35 million tonnes, 20 percent above the five-year average and almost twice the 2022 harvest.
scope: Morocco (the brief's country); 2023 barley output; brief of 26 July 2023
attribution: © FAO 2023 GIEWS Country Brief Morocco, reference date 26-July-2023
note: The brief of 21 March 2024 (gx-SCI-25-009) gives 1.3 million tonnes, 20 percent below the five-year average, for the same year. Both are kept as printed.

excerpt: Wheat and barley production in 2023 is estimated at 4.1 and 1.3 million tonnes, about 17 percent and 20 percent, respectively, below five-year average.
statement: The GIEWS brief of 21 March 2024 estimates 2023 wheat and barley production at 4.1 and 1.3 million tonnes, about 17 percent and 20 percent below the five-year average.
scope: Morocco (the brief's country); 2023 wheat and barley production; brief of 21 March 2024
attribution: © FAO 2024 GIEWS Country Brief Morocco, reference date 21-March-2024
note: Disagrees with the brief of 26 July 2023 on 2023 barley (gx-SCI-25-008).

excerpt: Cereal production in 2024 is estimated about 3.3 million tonnes, over 40 percent below-average.
statement: The GIEWS brief of 6 February 2025 estimates 2024 cereal production at about 3.3 million tonnes, over 40 percent below average.
scope: Morocco (the brief's country); 2024 cereal production; brief of 6 February 2025
attribution: © FAO 2025 GIEWS Country Brief Morocco, reference date 6-February-2025

excerpt: This marks the second consecutive year of drought conditions in the country
statement: The GIEWS brief of 23 July 2025 describes the 2024/25 winter rainfall deficit as the second consecutive year of drought conditions in Morocco.
scope: Morocco ('the country'); the 2024/25 winter season; brief of 23 July 2025
attribution: © FAO 2025 GIEWS Country Brief Morocco, reference date 23-July-2025

excerpt: Favourable early season conditions for cereal plantings in 2025/26
statement: The GIEWS brief of 2 February 2026 reports favourable early season conditions for the 2025/26 cereal plantings.
scope: Morocco (the brief's country); 2025/26 cereal plantings; brief of 2 February 2026
attribution: © FAO 2026 GIEWS Country Brief Morocco, reference date 02-February-2026

excerpt: Noting that more than half of the Earth’s land surface is classified as rangelands and that these areas are suffering considerable desertification
statement: In resolution 76/253 the UN General Assembly notes that more than half of the Earth's land surface is classified as rangelands and that these areas suffer considerable desertification.
scope: The Earth's land surface; no period stated
attribution: United Nations General Assembly (2022). International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists, 2026. Resolution A/RES/76/253.

excerpt: Decides to declare 2026 the International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists;
statement: In resolution 76/253 (2022) the UN General Assembly declared 2026 the International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists.
scope: Worldwide; the year 2026
attribution: United Nations General Assembly (2022). International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists, 2026. Resolution A/RES/76/253.

statement: The UNCCD report states that rangelands cover 80 million square kilometres, over 54 per cent of the terrestrial surface, the largest land cover or use type in the world.
scope: Rangelands worldwide; no period stated

statement: The UNCCD report states that rangelands support the livelihoods of approximately 2 billion people.
scope: Rangelands worldwide; no period stated

statement: The UNCCD report states that collecting data and monitoring rangelands can be expensive and hard, which makes rangeland health and trends difficult to assess.
scope: Rangelands in general; no period stated

excerpt: These three methods may be designated, first, the method of the ruling theory; second, the method of the working hypothesis; and, third, the method of multiple working hypotheses.
statement: Chamberlin distinguishes three methods: the ruling theory, the working hypothesis, and multiple working hypotheses.
scope: No place or period stated

excerpt: a premature explanation passes into a tentative theory, then into an adopted theory, and then into a ruling theory.
statement: Chamberlin describes how a premature explanation becomes a tentative theory, then an adopted theory, then a ruling theory.
scope: No place or period stated

excerpt: CHIRPS v3 combines satellite-based thermal infrared rainfall estimates (CHIRP) with in-situ station observations to produce a 0.05° gridded rainfall time series over land.
statement: CHIRPS v3 combines satellite thermal infrared rainfall estimates with station observations into a 0.05° gridded rainfall series over land.
scope: Land areas covered by CHIRPS v3; no period stated

excerpt: Two CHIRPS products are produced operationally: A rapid preliminary version, and a later final version.
statement: CHIRPS v3 is produced as a rapid preliminary version and a later final version.
scope: No place or period stated

excerpt: The European Space Agency (ESA) WorldCover 10 m 2021 product provides a global land cover map for 2021 at 10 m resolution based on Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 data.
statement: ESA WorldCover provides a global 10 m land cover map for 2021 based on Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 data.
scope: Global; the year 2021

excerpt: The terms of use for this dataset are CC-BY-4.0.
statement: The ESA WorldCover 2021 dataset is released under CC BY 4.0.
scope: No place or period stated

scope: Regional patterns of water availability; no period stated

excerpt: In the Ait Bouguemez Valley (High Atlas, Morocco), we examined how Amazigh women perceive, define and manage ethno‐habitats

scope: Ait Bouguemez Valley (High Atlas, Morocco); no period stated

excerpt: positive RUE-trends dominate in most of the Sahel, indicating that non-precipitation related land degradation is not a widespread phenomenon

scope: Most of the Sahel; no period stated in the excerpt

excerpt: Thirty-seven percent of the pixels in Sahel satisfy these requirements
statement: Thirty-seven percent of the Sahel pixels meet the two preconditions for a meaningful rain-use efficiency trend analysis.
scope: Sahel pixels; no period stated in the excerpt
